name: Ahikam
overview: Ahikam, identified as the son of Shaphan, appears prominently in the time of King Josiah's reforms, serving as a trusted official alongside priests and scribes who sought the Lord's guidance through the prophetess Huldah concerning the discovered Book of the Law (2 Kings 22:12-14; 2 Chronicles 34:20). His protective influence is notably seen in his intervention to save the prophet Jeremiah from death (Jeremiah 26:24), demonstrating a commitment to God's messengers. Furthermore, Ahikam's legacy continued through his son Gedaliah, who was appointed ruler over the remnant in Judah after the Babylonian exile began (2 Kings 25:22), highlighting Ahikam's enduring role in God's providential care for His people.
